title: The Vine Never Rejects the Branch
headline: Do You Have to Fix Yourself Before Coming Back to God?
headline_sub: The Vine Never Rejects the Branch
tagline: Healing almost always begins where hiding ends.
seo_title: Do You Have to Fix Yourself Before Returning to God? John 15:5 | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Shame says disconnect until you're worthy; Jesus says remain in Me. A devotional and men's group questions on John 15:5, 1 John 1:7, shame and brotherhood.
verse_text: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in Me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from Me you can do nothing.

scriptures.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in Me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from Me you can do nothing.
If we walk in the light, as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.

items: In John 15, Jesus never tells the branch, “Produce fruit first, then come back.”
He simply says, “Abide in Me.”
Fruit comes afterward.
Many men quietly reverse the order.
“I’ll come back after I fix myself.”
“I’ll pray after I stop struggling.”
“I’ll serve after I stop failing.”
That isn’t conviction.
That is shame pretending to be humility.
Shame always makes us believe we have to become worthy before we can return.
Jesus says the opposite.
Return first.
Transformation follows relationship.
Fruit follows abiding.
Walking in the light doesn’t mean you’ve become perfect.
It means you’ve stopped hiding.
It means you’ve stopped pretending.
It means you’ve brought what was hidden into the presence of Christ and the fellowship of trusted brothers.
That’s what biblical brotherhood was always meant to become.
Not a place where men perform.
A place where men are known.

blocks.text: Think about an area where you regularly struggle.
Am I fighting sin…. or am I fighting shame?

items: Those are not the same battle.
Sin resists obedience.
Shame resists intimacy.
One calls for repentance.
The other whispers that repentance won’t matter.
Shame says, “Disconnect until you’re worthy.”
Jesus says, “Remain in Me.”
The enemy isolates.
Grace invites fellowship.
Healing almost always begins where hiding ends.
What is the difference between conviction and condemnation?
How has shame affected your relationship with God and with others?
Why do men instinctively hide after they fail? What are they afraid might happen if they are fully known?
What does genuine biblical repentance actually look like? How is it different from simply feeling guilty?
How did Jesus consistently respond to broken people? What patterns do you see throughout the Gospels?
What area of your life today needs both grace and truth?
